messages:
Maya K: FYI I'm seeing a bunch of CUDA OOMs on us-east-1 serving nodes over the last ~10m. error logs show 'CUDA out of memory' even though allocator reports ~10% headroom.
Tom H: Repro? which model/seqlen?
Maya K: Mostly gpt-medium-16k running 2x batched requests, seqlen ~6k. Happens across a handful of containers on node gpu-ue1-112, gpu-ue1-115.
Arjun S: incident-bot created INC-2026-1782. Paging pd-oncall. Can someone check nvidia-smi + dmesg on the nodes?
infra-bot: @channel Incident INC-2026-1782 opened (severity: P2). Affected pool: us-east-1-serving.
pd-oncall: on it, rerouting traffic now.
Simone Lee: Running `ssh gpu-ue1-112` now. nvidia-smi looks normal, memory usage ~70% overall, but `dmesg` shows lines:
```
[  5432.123456] Out of memory: CUDA allocation failed: out of memory
[  5432.123789] allocator: reserved blocks 0x7f.., free headroom 512MB
[  5432.124001] uvmm: fragmentation detected, largest free 480MB
```
Maya K: that's the mismatch — allocator thinks headroom exists, but largest contiguous chunk < requested allocation. fragmentation + reserved block alignment causing spill.
Tom H: Any recent config changes to reserve size or quantization? I see a commit yesterday bumping RESERVED_BLOCK_CHUNKS from 16 to 24 for better reuse.
Arjun S: That bump could increase fragmentation with large mid-size allocations. Suggest temporary mitigation: reduce RESERVED_BLOCK_CHUNKS back to 12 and disable prefix KV cache on the affected pool to free contiguous areas.
Simone Lee: I can push a canary to gpu-ue1-115 with env `REDWOOD_ALLOC_RESERVED_CHUNKS=12` and `KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false` for one container. Want logs/tracing enabled.
pd-oncall: please migrate traffic off gpu-ue1-112 while we test, keep customer-impact flag updated. Notifying support to annotate impacted requests.
Maya K: running canary now on gpu-ue1-115. command: `kubectl set env deploy/serve-worker REDWOOD_ALLOC_RESERVED_CHUNKS=12 -n serving-us-east-1 --record && kubectl set env deploy/serve-worker KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false -n serving-us-east-1 --record`
Tom H: Watching metrics — token latency + OOM rate. If canary stabilizes for 5m, roll to remaining affected nodes.
infra-bot: Canary deployed to gpu-ue1-115 (pod serve-worker-7f9d).
Maya K: immediate effect: pod-level OOMs dropped to 0 on that pod; alloc logs show larger contiguous free block ~1.2GB now.
Arjun S: Great. Next mitigation: schedule rolling restart for gpu-ue1-112 after draining to defragment GPU memory, and apply reserved chunks change cluster-wide during low-traffic window. Also open a follow-up to evaluate allocator coalescing behavior when reserved blocks are increased.
Simone Lee: Noted. Raising ticket INFRA-alloc-2026 to evaluate defrag heuristics and track change history for reserved blocks.
Maya K: Customer impact: intermittent 5-10% error rate on some user requests for ~20m, routed gracefully to fallback models for most customers. Support notified and patched incidents in status page.
Tom H: Also observed one container crash that led to node pod flapping on gpu-ue1-112 — likely due to multiple containers hitting fragmentation simultaneously. Drained node, cordoned for further debugging.
pd-oncall: node cordoned, traffic drained. continuing monitoring.
Arjun S: Postmortem action items: (1) revert reserved chunk bump until allocator defrag improved, (2) add continuous fragmentation metric (largest-contiguous-free), (3) improve KV cache eviction policy to prefer freeing large blocks, (4) run a stress test for high-seqlen workloads and measure failure modes.
Maya K: I'll draft incident summary and share with product + support. Thanks all — incident status: mitigated, monitoring. :white_check_mark:
Simone Lee: assigning follow-ups in INFRA board, marking this incident for deeper allocator investigation.
